grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; the proof is complete and correct.
grade.summary: The submission gives a valid well-founded lexicographic descent using the number of entries greater than 1 and the total sum of prime exponents, proving termination and preservation of at least one nonunit. It then correctly proves that, prime by prime, the gcd of all valuation exponents is invariant and reconstructs the unique terminal integer from these invariants.
strengths: Correctly computes the valuation transformation as (a,b) -> (min(a,b), |a-b|).
The lexicographic descent (N,S) handles both coprime and non-coprime moves and proves finite termination.
Correctly argues that every move preserves the existence of at least one entry greater than 1, so a terminal board has exactly one such entry.
The primewise gcd invariant is proved in both directions and correctly identifies every exponent of the terminal integer.
The resulting formula for M depends only on the initial board, establishing choice-independence.
